description: The gitea repo is a colocated jj repo (since 2026-10-24) with course-safe config; the local /jj skill holds the workflows.

On 2026-10-24 the user had me colocate jj 0.46 (from their Nix profile) in `/Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea`. The repo config is:
- `immutable_heads()` includes `remote_bookmarks()`, so pushed commits can't be rewritten.
- `user.name = "Ethan Turner"`, matching their git commits. The email comes from the global jj config (noreply).
- `snapshot.auto-track = "~root:ai-logs"`, so log files never get swept into a feature change.

The workflows live in the local skill `.claude/skills/jj/` (gitignored). `/file-ai-logs` points to it.

**Why:** The user wanted jj, but the course forbids force-push, rebase after review and squash, and wants approval for every commit. I tested on 2026-10-24 that without the immutability guard, `jj git push` silently force-pushes rewritten commits ("move sideways"). With it, describe and squash on pushed commits fail.

**How to apply:** Use `/jj` for every commit, branch, push or PR in this repo. A commit is `jj commit` after approval, followed by `jj bookmark set <branch> -r @-`. PRs use `gh pr create --head <bookmark>`. `git status` showing `HEAD (no branch)` is normal. Inside a Claude Code git worktree (`.claude/worktrees/`), jj answers for the main checkout, which I confirmed on 0.46. So there the skill uses plain git after approval, renaming the branch to the course name and never force-pushing. The user chose this over stopping on 2026-10-24.

Findings that shaped the skill (tested 2026-10-24):
- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch`** closes PRs based on that branch. The course repo has `delete_branch_on_merge=false`.
- **Dependent issues:** COURSE-WORKFLOW forbids merging feature branches into each other. I first wrongly suggested stacking #60 on #57. The rule is to build #60 locally without pushing, then rebase that unpushed work onto `main` after #57 merges. See [[sprint2-deliverables]] and [[commit-and-pr-conventions]].

#56 is ab-wm's central keyboard-shortcut registry. The user's #57 (`?` dialog), #60 (turn shortcuts off) and #95 (`r` quote reply) all build on it. #65 does not, so it can start first. See [[sprint2-deliverables]].

**Merged 2026-10-19** via PR #96 (as of 10-22 ab-wm's open PR #97 for #58 adds `initShortcutLink`, an additive change), so #57, #58, #59 and #95 are unblocked; #60 is still blocked by #57. Branch from `main` now.

**State on 2026-10-18 (history):** the code was on branch `origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, with the last commit on 10-18. It had no PR and was not merged. ab-wm's spec reviews on all four issues said to "pay attention to the changes introduced by #56".

**API on that branch** (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`):
- `registerShortcut({keys, description, section?, element?, action})` registers a shortcut. `keys` is a space-separated sequence, such as `"g c"`. `description` and `section` arrive already translated from the server, through data attributes or a placeholder. A shortcut with an `element` lives only while that element is connected. Exact or prefix clashes throw.
- `getShortcuts()` returns the list that #57's dialog reads.
- `handleKeyDown` is the only dispatch point, where #60's off switch goes. It skips inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable, modifier keys, and events another handler already prevented.
- `initShortcutKbd` registers `s` and `t` from `<kbd>` hints, under the section "Repository". Nothing registers `?` yet.
- Unit tests are in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.

**Why:** ab-wm owns #56, and the API can change before it merges. The specs for #57, #60 and #95 name these functions, so a rename means updating those issue bodies too.

**How to apply:** before implementing #57, #60 or #95, check the state live. Use `gh pr list --search 56` and `git log origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, and re-read `shortcut.ts`. Branch from `main` only after #56 merges; never merge ab-wm's branch into the user's own branch (COURSE-WORKFLOW). If #56 is late, raise it with ab-wm early, because a sprint with no merged PR scores 0.

AGENTS.md has the base rules: Conventional Commits, the `Assisted-by:` trailer only, approval for each commit, and the issue number in the subject. Beyond those:

- **Trailer form:** `Assisted-by: Claude Code:<session model id>`, for example `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5`.
- **Editing a PR body:** `gh pr edit --body-file` replaces the whole body. Keep the `Closes #N` line and any image URLs.
- **Tech Debt section (from Sprint 2):** every PR body needs `## Tech Debt` with `**Introduced:**` and `**Encountered:**` lines; "None." is valid. Missing it costs D4 points. See [[sprint2-requirements]].
- **Screenshots required:** `CONTRIBUTING.md` wants UI screenshots on PRs. Show "after" only for a new feature, and before and after otherwise.

Hosting screenshots:
- `gh` can't mint `github.com/user-attachments/...` URLs; only the web UI uploads there.
- Commit the images under `docs/sprint<N>/screenshots/` (since 2026-10-24). Not under `ai-logs/`: `.coderabbit.yaml`'s PR-description check fails any link into `ai-logs/`, screenshots included (it flagged PR #115; Sprint 1's #71/#74 predate the check).
- Reference them as `https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/<full-commit-sha>/<path>?raw=1`. Use the SHA as pushed: a squash or describe before the push changes it, and the old link 404s. Pin the SHA, not the branch, so the images survive branch deletion.

Taking screenshots (done for PR #71):
- Use headless Chromium with `colorScheme: 'light' | 'dark'` and `deviceScaleFactor: 2`, then `page.screenshot` with a `clip`.
- Read each image back to check the crop.
- Rebuild first, or the footer shows a stale version.
- After pushing, confirm each `?raw=1` URL returns 200 as an image.

**Why:** The course fork diverges from default attribution, and these screenshot details each cost a retry.
**How to apply:** Use with [[verify-skill]] for the capture. Commit identity is in [[course-repo-and-identity]].

`r` quotes selected text into the reply box on issue and pull request pages
> Sub-issue of #23 · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged) · AC7's dialog listing needs #57

## User Story
As a user who replies on an issue or a pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote my selected text into my reply, or to take me to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer reads a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom. The sentence is already in the box as a Markdown quote, and the cursor is after it, ready for typing. Later, the maintainer is back at the top of the thread with nothing selected. They press `r` again and land in the same reply box, with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, `r` does nothing. Archived repositories and signed-out visitors are two examples.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes the text into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside one comment | Moves to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside one comment or inside the issue description, on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box gets the text as a Markdown quote, with `> ` at the start of each line. The box scrolls into view, and the cursor is after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text stays, and the quote follows it after a blank line.
- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment, or the selection is outside every comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view. The cursor is at the end of the box's text, and the text does not change.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box shows its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then the box switches back to the Write tab, so the cursor and any quote are visible.
- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box, when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error appears. Pages with no reply box include an archived repository, any page for a signed-out visitor, and a locked conversation that the user cannot comment on.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or in any other text field, when the user types `r`, then an `r` character appears in the field.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed by `getShortcuts()` or #57's dialog, then `r` has the description from the existing locale key `repo.issues.context.quote_reply`, and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests cover the selection check in AC1 and AC3. A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1 and AC5 and calls `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Comments in code review threads, and the reply boxes of those threads.
- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts: `a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`.
- GitHub's `c` shortcuts. #59 adds them.
- Escape to leave the reply box. Tab already leaves it.
- Submitting the comment. `Ctrl+Enter` and `Cmd+Enter` already submit it, and this issue does not change them.
- Changes to what the "Quote reply" item in each comment's menu does.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user. #57 adds the dialog that does this.

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: share one quoting helper with the "Quote reply" menu item
**Decision:** Move the shared part of the existing "Quote reply" handler, `tryOnQuoteReply` in `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`, into a helper. The helper takes a comment's content element and the reply editor. It appends the quoted selection, focuses the editor, and moves the cursor to the end. The menu item and `r` both call the helper.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) `r` finds the comment that holds the selection, and clicks that comment's "Quote reply" menu item from code.
- (b) A separate handler for `r` with its own copy of the code that converts the selection to Markdown and appends it.

**Rationale:** Option (a) needs no refactor, but it ties `r` to the comment menu's markup and to the `data-target` lookup in the menu's click handler. A change to the menu, such as the `<aria-menu>` migration work under #25, would break `r` without any change to the code for `r`. Option (b) keeps two copies of the quoting code. A fix to one copy would miss the other. One example is the lossy HTML-to-Markdown conversion that a comment in `repo-issue-edit.ts` notes. With a shared helper, there is one copy of the quoting code, and the menu item keeps its current behaviour.

**Consequences:** The change touches the existing quote-reply code, so this issue must check that code's behaviour, by hand or with a test. The helper also switches the reply box back to the Write tab (AC4). The menu item does not do this today, so the menu item gets the same fix.

### Decision 2: register `r` only on pages with a reply box
**Decision:** Register `r` only when the page has a reply editor (`#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor`), and pass that editor as the shortcut's `element` to #56's `registerShortcut`. The template puts `data-*` attributes on `#comment-form` that hold the translated description and section label of `r`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Register `r` on every issue and pull request page, and make its action return early when the page has no reply box.
- (b) Register `r` from a `<kbd>` hint in the template, the way #56 registers `s` and `t`.

**Rationale:** The server already decides whether to render the reply form. It checks that the user is signed in, that the repository is not archived, and that the user may comment on a locked conversation. Registration that depends on the form gives AC5, with no permission logic in JavaScript. With option (a), #57's dialog lists `r` on pages where `r` does nothing. Option (b) adds a visible hint to the reply box. GitHub shows no such hint, and this design does not need one.

**Consequences:** `r` and its row in the dialog exist only on pages where `r` works. If a future template renders the reply form on a page where the user cannot post, `r` still registers there. Registration follows the form, not the user's permission.

## Scope
small (2 points)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/everick/Projects/CSCI435/gitea/.claude/skills/jj

# jj in the course repo

This repo is colocated: `.jj/` sits beside `.git/`. jj is the tool you drive, and git, GitHub and `gh` still see normal branches and commits. jj's bookmarks are git's branches.

Course rules from `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md` and `AGENTS.md` still apply word for word. jj changes the commands, not the rules:

- One issue per branch, named `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-…` or `chore/…`.
- Commit messages are Conventional Commits ending in `(#N)`, plus an `Assisted-by: Claude Code:<model id>` trailer. Never add `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by`.
- **A human approves every commit before it's made.** Approval doesn't carry over to later commits.
- Pick up new `main` work by merging it into your branch, never by rebasing. Never rebase or squash once review has started, and never force-push.
- Never merge another feature branch into yours. PRs target `main`.

## Before any jj command: are you in a git worktree?

Claude Code's isolated agents and `EnterWorktree` work in plain git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/`. Those have no `.jj/` of their own, so jj climbs up and answers for the main checkout instead. Tested on jj 0.46: in a worktree with a modified and a new file, `jj st` said "The working copy has no changes", and `jj describe` rewrote the main checkout's change.

So check first:

```bash
[ "$(jj root 2>/dev/null)" = "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" ] || echo "in a git worktree: don't use jj"
```

If they differ, you're in a git worktree. Run no jj commands there, and use plain git with the course rules applied by hand, because jj's immutability guard doesn't reach this checkout:

1. Tell the user you're in a git worktree and will use plain git.
2. Check the branch name with `git branch --show-current`. A harness name such as `worktree-agent-57` breaks the course naming, so rename it first: `git branch -m feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog`.
3. Show the message and `git diff --stat` (with new files listed from `git status --short`), then wait for approval. Commit only the files that belong to the change: `git add <paths>`, then `git commit -m "<message>"` with the `Assisted-by` trailer after a blank line.
4. Push with `git push -u origin <branch>`. Never pass `--force` or `--force-with-lease`, and never amend or rebase anything already pushed. A fix goes in a new commit.

## Never open an editor

A jj command that opens `$EDITOR` or a merge tool waits for input an agent never sends, and hangs. Always pass the message or the paths:

- `jj describe -m`, `jj commit -m`, and `jj new -m` when you want a message.
- `jj squash --from <rev> --into <rev> -m`, and `jj split <paths> -m`.
- Never run bare `jj describe`, `jj commit`, `jj squash -i`, `jj split`, `jj diffedit` or `jj resolve`.

## The repo's jj config (already set)

`jj config list --repo` should show:

```
revset-aliases."trunk()" = "main@origin"
revset-aliases."immutable_heads()" = "builtin_immutable_heads() | remote_bookmarks()"
user.name = "Ethan Turner"
snapshot.auto-track = "~root:ai-logs"
```

- **`immutable_heads()`** makes every pushed commit immutable, so `jj describe`, `jj squash`, `jj rebase` and `jj abandon` on pushed work fail with "Commit … is immutable". This is the guard that keeps the no-rewrite rule. Without it, `jj git push` silently force-pushes a rewritten commit, reporting it as "move sideways". Never pass `--ignore-immutable`. If a command hits the guard, the right move is a new commit on top.
- **`snapshot.auto-track`** keeps new files under `ai-logs/` out of whatever change you're on, because jj otherwise records every new file automatically. Add logs on purpose with `jj file track <paths>`.
- The email comes from the user's global jj config (the GitHub noreply address). Never commit with the wm.edu address.

If any of these are missing, restore them with `jj config set --repo …`. To quote a fileset, write `'"~root:ai-logs"'`.

## What a "commit" is in jj

The working copy is always a commit (`@`), and jj saves your edits into it automatically. A course "commit" means sealing `@` with a message: `jj commit -m "<message>"`. That gives `@` its description and starts a fresh empty `@` on top.

Before running `jj commit`, show the user the message and `jj diff --stat` (or the full `jj diff`), then wait for approval. Write the message with the trailer after a blank line:

```bash
jj commit -m "feat(shortcut): open a help dialog with ? (#57)

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5"
```

The commit is now `@-`. Move the branch to it with `jj bookmark set <branch> -r @-`. Bookmarks don't follow new commits on their own, and an unmoved bookmark pushes stale code.

## Workflows

**Start an issue.** This replaces `git switch main; git pull; git switch -c`:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new main@origin                                # empty change on fresh main
# ...edit, then commit with approval as above...
jj bookmark create feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
```

**Push and open the PR.** Push one named bookmark at a time, never `--all`:

```bash
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
gh pr create --head feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog --base main --title "…" --body-file <file>
```

Read the push output. `add to` and `move forward` are fine. `move sideways` or `move backward` means history was rewritten: stop and tell the user before anything else happens.

`gh pr create` always needs `--head`. git has no current branch in a jj repo (`git status` says `HEAD (no branch)`), so `gh` can't infer it. The PR body uses the course format from `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, including `## Tech Debt` and `Closes #N`.

**Review follow-ups.** Add new commits on top. Never amend or squash:

```bash
jj new feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
# ...edit, then commit with approval...
jj bookmark set feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
```

**Sync with main.** Merge, don't rebase. The merge is itself a commit, so the user approves it too:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog main@origin -m "Merge branch 'main' into feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog

Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5"
jj new                                            # seal the merge
jj bookmark set feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog -r @-
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
```

Like every commit, the merge carries the `Assisted-by` trailer.

If the merge has conflicts, `jj st` lists them. Resolve them by editing the conflict markers in the files (not with `jj resolve`, which opens a merge tool), run `jj st` to confirm none remain, then push.

**Rewording or tidying work you haven't pushed.** `jj describe`, `jj squash` and `jj split` are allowed on commits that were never pushed, because review hasn't started on them. The immutability guard tells you where that line is.

**Issues that depend on each other** (#60 needs #57). Never base a PR on another feature branch and never merge #57's branch into #60's. You may build #60 locally on top of #57 without pushing it or giving it a bookmark. Once #57 merges into `main`, move the unpushed #60 work onto `main` (a rebase is allowed here because nothing was pushed), then bookmark and push it:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj rebase -s <first #60 change> -d main@origin
jj bookmark create feat/issue-60-… -r <last #60 change>
```

**Review a teammate's PR.** Look at it without making a git branch:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new feat/issue-59-c-shortcuts@origin          # their branch, read-only to you
# build, run /verify, read the code
jj new main@origin                                # leave; jj drops the empty change
```

**Commit AI logs.** Files under `ai-logs/` aren't tracked until you say so. Follow `/file-ai-logs` for naming and the issue comment. Then, on the branch the log belongs to:

```bash
jj new <branch>                                   # or main@origin for a chore/ai-log-… branch
jj file track ai-logs/sprint2/controlled-opposition/<log files>
jj commit -m "chore(ai-log): add <slug> (#N)"     # with approval
jj bookmark set <branch> -r @-
```

**After the PR merges.** This replaces `git switch main; git pull; git branch -d; git push --delete`:

```bash
jj git fetch
jj new main@origin
jj bookmark delete feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog
jj git push -b feat/issue-57-shortcut-help-dialog        # pushes the deletion to GitHub
```

Deleting the remote branch is outward-facing, so run that push as its own command after the user's OK. If a permission check blocks it, stop and hand the command to the user; don't try another route.

## Traps found in testing

- **`gh pr merge --delete-branch` closes PRs that target the deleted branch.** It doesn't retarget them, and this repo has GitHub's automatic head-branch deletion off. Course PRs target `main`, so this only matters if someone breaks that rule.
- **Tools that read git:**
  - Claude Code's git status and `git status` will show `HEAD (no branch)`. That's normal.
  - `/verify`'s doctor still checks build freshness against `HEAD`.
  - In the main checkout, don't run `git commit`, `git checkout`, `git rebase` or `git merge` (a git worktree is the one exception, above): jj imports their effects, but they bypass the immutability guard and the approval flow. Read-only git commands (`git log`, `git diff`, `git show`) are fine.
- **jj 0.46 CLI differences:** global flags like `--quiet` go before the subcommand, and `jj git push --allow-new` no longer exists (new bookmarks push without it).

## Undo

`jj undo` reverses the last jj operation, and `jj op log` lists every operation so `jj op restore <id>` can roll back further. Both work only locally. Undoing after a push leaves GitHub unchanged, and the next push would then be a force-push. So if a pushed state is wrong, fix it with a new commit, never by undoing and pushing again.

import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  private shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  private pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  private pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.trim().split(/\s+/).join(' ').toLowerCase(); // "g  c" would otherwise never match a press
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);
  registerShortcut({
    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

// a link declares a shortcut that goes where it leads, described separately because its text may hold more, e.g. a count
export function initShortcutLink(link: HTMLAnchorElement) {
  registerShortcut({
    keys: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: link,
    action: () => window.location.assign(link.getAttribute('data-shortcut-href') ?? link.href), // e.g. "g c" goes to the default branch, not the browsed one
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}

export function initGlobalShortcut() {
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onGlobalShortcut', initShortcutKbd);
  registerGlobalInitFunc('onShortcutLink', initShortcutLink);
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => globalRegistry.handleKeyDown(e));

  // A <kbd> element next to an <input> declares a keyboard shortcut for that input.
  // initShortcutKbd registers it, so pressing the matching key focuses the sibling input.
  // When Escape is pressed inside such an input, the input is cleared and blurred.
  // The <kbd> element is shown/hidden automatically based on input focus and value.
  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    // Ctrl/Alt/Cmd+Escape is left alone
    if (e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey) return;

    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;

    // Handle Escape: clear and blur inputs that have an associated keyboard shortcut
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      const kbd = kbdFromElem(target);
      if (kbd) {
        (target as HTMLInputElement).value = '';
        (target as HTMLInputElement).blur();
      }
    }
  });

  // Toggle kbd shortcut hint visibility on input focus/blur
  document.addEventListener('focusin', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    hideElem(kbd);
  });

  document.addEventListener('focusout', (e) => {
    const kbd = kbdFromElem(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (!kbd) return;
    const hasContent = Boolean((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
    toggleElem(kbd, !hasContent);
  });
}

import {handleReply} from './repo-issue.ts';
import {getComboMarkdownEditor, initComboMarkdownEditor, ComboMarkdownEditor} from './comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts';
import {POST} from '../modules/fetch.ts';
import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';
import {hideElem, querySingleVisibleElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {errorMessage} from '../modules/errors.ts';
import {triggerUploadStateChanged} from './comp/EditorUpload.ts';
import {convertHtmlToMarkdown} from '../markup/html2markdown.ts';
import {applyAreYouSure, reinitializeAreYouSure} from '../vendor/jquery.are-you-sure.ts';

async function tryOnEditContent(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.edit-content');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const commentContent = clickTarget.closest('.comment-header')!.nextElementSibling!;
  const editContentZone = commentContent.querySelector('.edit-content-zone')!;
  let renderContent = commentContent.querySelector('.render-content')!;
  const rawContent = commentContent.querySelector('.raw-content')!;

  let comboMarkdownEditor : ComboMarkdownEditor;

  const cancelAndReset = (e: Event) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    showElem(renderContent);
    hideElem(editContentZone);
    comboMarkdownEditor.dropzoneReloadFiles();
  };

  const saveAndRefresh = async (e: Event) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    // we are already in a form, do not bubble up to the document otherwise there will be other "form submit handlers"
    // at the moment, the form submit event conflicts with initRepoDiffConversationForm (global '.conversation-holder form' event handler)
    e.stopPropagation();
    renderContent.classList.add('is-loading');
    showElem(renderContent);
    hideElem(editContentZone);
    try {
      const params = new URLSearchParams({
        content: comboMarkdownEditor.value(),
        context: String(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-context')),
        content_version: String(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-content-version')),
      });
      for (const file of comboMarkdownEditor.dropzoneGetFiles() ?? []) {
        params.append('files[]', file);
      }

      const response = await POST(editContentZone.getAttribute('data-update-url')!, {data: params});
      const data = await response.json();
      if (!response.ok) {
        showErrorToast(data?.errorMessage ?? window.config.i18n.error_occurred);
        return;
      }

      reinitializeAreYouSure(editContentZone.querySelector('form')); // the form is no longer dirty
      editContentZone.setAttribute('data-content-version', data.contentVersion);

      // replace the render content with new one, to trigger re-initialization of all features
      const newRenderContent = renderContent.cloneNode(false) as HTMLElement;
      newRenderContent.innerHTML = data.content;
      renderContent.replaceWith(newRenderContent);
      renderContent = newRenderContent;

      rawContent.textContent = comboMarkdownEditor.value();

      if (!commentContent.querySelector('.dropzone-attachments')) {
        if (data.attachments !== '') {
          commentContent.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', data.attachments);
        }
      } else if (data.attachments === '') {
        commentContent.querySelector('.dropzone-attachments')!.remove();
      } else {
        commentContent.querySelector('.dropzone-attachments')!.outerHTML = data.attachments;
      }
      comboMarkdownEditor.dropzoneSubmitReload();
    } catch (error) {
      showErrorToast(`Failed to save the content: ${errorMessage(error)}`);
      console.error(error);
    } finally {
      renderContent.classList.remove('is-loading');
    }
  };

  // Show write/preview tab and copy raw content as needed
  showElem(editContentZone);
  hideElem(renderContent);

  comboMarkdownEditor = getComboMarkdownEditor(editContentZone.querySelector('.combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  if (!comboMarkdownEditor) {
    editContentZone.innerHTML = document.querySelector('#issue-comment-editor-template')!.innerHTML;
    const form = editContentZone.querySelector('form')!;
    applyAreYouSure(form);
    const saveButton = querySingleVisibleElem<HTMLButtonElement>(editContentZone, '.ui.primary.button')!;
    const cancelButton = querySingleVisibleElem<HTMLButtonElement>(editContentZone, '.ui.cancel.button')!;
    comboMarkdownEditor = await initComboMarkdownEditor(editContentZone.querySelector('.combo-markdown-editor')!);
    const syncUiState = () => saveButton.disabled = comboMarkdownEditor.isUploading();
    comboMarkdownEditor.container.addEventListener(ComboMarkdownEditor.EventUploadStateChanged, syncUiState);
    cancelButton.addEventListener('click', cancelAndReset);
    form.addEventListener('submit', saveAndRefresh);
  }
  // when the content has changed on server side, there is no sync, and this page doesn't have the latest content,
  // the editor still shows the old content, server will reject end user's submit by "data-content-version" check
  comboMarkdownEditor.value(rawContent.textContent);
  comboMarkdownEditor.switchTabToEditor();
  comboMarkdownEditor.focus();
  triggerUploadStateChanged(comboMarkdownEditor.container);
}

function extractSelectedMarkdown(container: HTMLElement) {
  const selection = window.getSelection();
  if (!selection?.rangeCount) return '';
  const range = selection.getRangeAt(0);
  if (!container.contains(range.commonAncestorContainer)) return '';

  // todo: if commonAncestorContainer parent has "[data-markdown-original-content]" attribute, use the parent's markdown content
  // otherwise, use the selected HTML content and respect all "[data-markdown-original-content]/[data-markdown-generated-content]" attributes
  const contents = selection.getRangeAt(0).cloneContents();
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.append(contents);
  return convertHtmlToMarkdown(el);
}

async function tryOnQuoteReply(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.quote-reply');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const contentToQuoteId = clickTarget.getAttribute('data-target');
  const targetRawToQuote = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${contentToQuoteId}.raw-content`)!;
  const targetMarkupToQuote = targetRawToQuote.parentElement!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup')!;
  let contentToQuote = extractSelectedMarkdown(targetMarkupToQuote);
  if (!contentToQuote) contentToQuote = targetRawToQuote.textContent;
  const quotedContent = `${contentToQuote.replace(/^/mg, '> ')}\n\n`;

  let editor;
  if (clickTarget.classList.contains('quote-reply-diff')) {
    const replyBtn = clickTarget.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.comment-form-reply')!;
    editor = await handleReply(replyBtn);
  } else {
    // for normal issue/comment page
    editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  }

  if (editor.value()) {
    editor.value(`${editor.value()}\n\n${quotedContent}`);
  } else {
    editor.value(quotedContent);
  }
  editor.focus();
  editor.moveCursorToEnd();
}

export function initRepoIssueCommentEdit() {
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    tryOnEditContent(e); // Edit issue or comment content
    tryOnQuoteReply(e); // Quote reply to the comment editor
  });
}

# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |
| `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` | `registerShortcut` (keys like `'g c'`), `getShortcuts`, and the `<kbd data-shortcut-keys data-shortcut-section>` hints and `onShortcutLink` links that register themselves |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already on many pages, not new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** `?_ui_performance_trace=1` prints per-init timings; over 500ms is logged.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read

345:+{"assignees":["controlled-opposition"],"body":"\u003e Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56\n\n## User Story\nAs a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.\n\n## User Scenario\nA user is on a repository's home page and presses `?`. A dialog titled \"Keyboard shortcuts\" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under \"General\". It lists `S` (\"Search code…\") and `T` (\"Go to file\") under \"Repository\". Each row shows the keys as `\u003ckbd\u003e` elements next to the description. Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab never reaches the page behind it. The user presses Escape. The dialog closes, and focus returns to where it was.\n\nOn the notifications page, no shortcuts belong to the page itself. There, `?` opens the same dialog and lists only `?`.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, and focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled \"Keyboard shortcuts\" opens. It has one row for each shortcut that #56's `getShortcuts()` returns on that page, with the shortcut's keys and description.\n- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then the dialog closes and focus returns to the element that had focus before the dialog opened.\n- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus never reaches a control on the page behind the dialog.\n- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, a textarea or an editable area, when the user types `?`, then a `?` character appears in the field and the dialog does not open.\n- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut that later code registers with a new section appears under that section, with no change to the dialog's code.\n- [ ] AC6: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the title, the close button's accessible name and the \"General\" heading come from locale keys.\n- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again, then the dialog stays open and unchanged, and no error occurs.\n- [ ] AC8: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses the key of another shortcut on the page, then that shortcut does not run. For example, `s` on a repository home page does not move focus to the code search box.\n- [ ] AC9: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC8 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`. Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Shortcuts other than `?`. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59, and `r` is #95. Each one appears in the dialog when its issue registers it.\n- Shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog lists only what works on the current page.\n- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.\n- The setting that turns shortcuts off. #60 adds that setting to this dialog as a checkbox.\n- A link to the dialog in the footer or in a menu.\n- A printable list or a documentation page of shortcuts.\n\n## Open Questions\n- Should the user also be able to open the dialog with the mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue. One way in keeps the e2e test complete.\n- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? Proposed: no. Escape and the close button are then the only ways out. Reviewer to confirm.\n\n## Design Decision\n\n### Decision 1: build the dialog on the native `\u003cdialog\u003e` element\n**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `\u003cdialog\u003e` element and open it with `showModal()`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) A Fomantic modal that `showFomanticModal` in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts` opens. Gitea's other modals use this today.\n- (b) A plain `\u003cdiv\u003e` with a focus trap, a backdrop and an Escape handler written by hand.\n\n**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and that new features must not use it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal in an accessibility feature works against #25. `showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert (AC3), closes the dialog on Escape (AC2) and sets `aria-modal`. Option (b) would rewrite behaviour that the browser already has, and hand-written focus handling causes the kind of bug that #25 fixes.\n\n**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `\u003cdialog\u003e` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.\n\n### Decision 2: render the dialog's markup and text on the server\n**Decision:** Render the empty `\u003cdialog\u003e` once in the base page template, next to the footer script, and keep it hidden until it opens. The server renders the translated title, close label and \"General\" heading. When the user presses `?`, JavaScript adds the rows from `getShortcuts()`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.\n- (b) A Vue component that mounts on demand and receives its strings as `data-locale-*` attributes.\n\n**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. But (a) splits the dialog's text between two mechanisms, and it builds markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.\n\n**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `s` and `t` shortcuts register from a `\u003ckbd\u003e` hint on the page, but `?` has no hint. JavaScript registers `?` instead, and reads its description and \"General\" label from data attributes on the dialog.\n\n## Scope\nmedium (5 points)\n\n---\n*Spec refined with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), reviewed and posted by @controlled-opposition.*\n","comments":[{"author":"ab-wm","body":"Spec reviewed: \nI do not see anything wrong with the specs, though do note that claude-students documentation are as accurate as they can, but can be incorrect in the finer details."}],"state":"OPEN","title":"`?` opens a shortcut help dialog built from the registry"}
363:+{"assignees":["controlled-opposition"],"body":"\u003e Sub-issue of #23 · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged) · AC7's dialog listing needs #57\n\n## User Story\nAs a user who replies on an issue or a pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote my selected text into my reply, or to take me to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.\n\n## User Scenario\nA maintainer reads a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom. The sentence is already in the box as a Markdown quote, and the cursor is after it, ready for typing. Later, the maintainer is back at the top of the thread with nothing selected. They press `r` again and land in the same reply box, with their text still there.\n\nOn a page with no reply box, `r` does nothing. Archived repositories and signed-out visitors are two examples.\n\n| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |\n| --- | --- |\n| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes the text into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |\n| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside one comment | Moves to the reply box |\n| No reply box on the page | Nothing |\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside one comment or inside the issue description, on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box gets the text as a Markdown quote, with `\u003e ` at the start of each line. The box scrolls into view, and the cursor is after the quote.\n- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text stays, and the quote follows it after a blank line.\n- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment, or the selection is outside every comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view. The cursor is at the end of the box's text, and the text does not change.\n- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box shows its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then the box switches back to the Write tab, so the cursor and any quote are visible.\n- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box, when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error appears. Pages with no reply box include an archived repository, any page for a signed-out visitor, and a locked conversation that the user cannot comment on.\n- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or in any other text field, when the user types `r`, then an `r` character appears in the field.\n- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed by `getShortcuts()` or #57's dialog, then `r` has the description from the existing locale key `repo.issues.context.quote_reply`, and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.\n- [ ] AC8: Unit tests cover the selection check in AC1 and AC3. A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1 and AC5 and calls `assertNoJsError`.\n\n## Out of Scope\n- Comments in code review threads, and the reply boxes of those threads.\n- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts: `a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`.\n- GitHub's `c` shortcuts. #59 adds them.\n- Escape to leave the reply box. Tab already leaves it.\n- Submitting the comment. `Ctrl+Enter` and `Cmd+Enter` already submit it, and this issue does not change them.\n- Changes to what the \"Quote reply\" item in each comment's menu does.\n- Showing the shortcuts to the user. #57 adds the dialog that does this.\n\n## Open Questions\n- None.\n\n## Design Decision\n\n### Decision 1: share one quoting helper with the \"Quote reply\" menu item\n**Decision:** Move the shared part of the existing \"Quote reply\" handler, `tryOnQuoteReply` in `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`, into a helper. The helper takes a comment's content element and the reply editor. It appends the quoted selection, focuses the editor, and moves the cursor to the end. The menu item and `r` both call the helper.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) `r` finds the comment that holds the selection, and clicks that comment's \"Quote reply\" menu item from code.\n- (b) A separate handler for `r` with its own copy of the code that converts the selection to Markdown and appends it.\n\n**Rationale:** Option (a) needs no refactor, but it ties `r` to the comment menu's markup and to the `data-target` lookup in the menu's click handler. A change to the menu, such as the `\u003caria-menu\u003e` migration work under #25, would break `r` without any change to the code for `r`. Option (b) keeps two copies of the quoting code. A fix to one copy would miss the other. One example is the lossy HTML-to-Markdown conversion that a comment in `repo-issue-edit.ts` notes. With a shared helper, there is one copy of the quoting code, and the menu item keeps its current behaviour.\n\n**Consequences:** The change touches the existing quote-reply code, so this issue must check that code's behaviour, by hand or with a test. The helper also switches the reply box back to the Write tab (AC4). The menu item does not do this today, so the menu item gets the same fix.\n\n### Decision 2: register `r` only on pages with a reply box\n**Decision:** Register `r` only when the page has a reply editor (`#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor`), and pass that editor as the shortcut's `element` to #56's `registerShortcut`. The template puts `data-*` attributes on `#comment-form` that hold the translated description and section label of `r`.\n\n**Alternatives Considered:**\n- (a) Register `r` on every issue and pull request page, and make its action return early when the page has no reply box.\n- (b) Register `r` from a `\u003ckbd\u003e` hint in the template, the way #56 registers `s` and `t`.\n\n**Rationale:** The server already decides whether to render the reply form. It checks that the user is signed in, that the repository is not archived, and that the user may comment on a locked conversation. Registration that depends on the form gives AC5, with no permission logic in JavaScript. With option (a), #57's dialog lists `r` on pages where `r` does nothing. Option (b) adds a visible hint to the reply box. GitHub shows no such hint, and this design does not need one.\n\n**Consequences:** `r` and its row in the dialog exist only on pages where `r` works. If a future template renders the reply form on a page where the user cannot post, `r` still registers there. Registration follows the form, not the user's permission.\n\n## Scope\nsmall (2 points)\n\n---\n*Spec refined with Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5), reviewed and posted by @controlled-opposition.*\n","comments":[{"author":"ab-wm","body":"### AI Assistance — @ab-wm \n\n**Role in this issue:** Issue drafting\n\n| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | claude-code | [TODO](ai-logs/sprint1/abhoot/2026-09-08_claude-web_understanding-issue-42.md) | Issue rewrite and code implementation details |\n\n(Will be updated in the future)\n\n"},{"author":"ab-wm","body":"Spec reviewed: All good, and not much different from what I had done.   value(v?: any) {
    if (v === undefined) {
      if (this.easyMDE) {
        return this.easyMDE.value();
      }
      return this.textarea.value;
    }

    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.value(v);
    } else {
      this.textarea.value = v;
    }
    this.textareaAutosize?.resizeToFit();
  }

  focus() {
    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.focus();
    } else {
      this.textarea.focus();
    }
  }

  moveCursorToEnd() {
    this.textarea.focus();
    this.textarea.setSelectionRange(this.textarea.value.length, this.textarea.value.length);
    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.focus();
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.setCursor(this.easyMDE.codemirror.lineCount(), 0);
    }
  }

import {env} from 'node:process';
import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test';
import type {Page} from '@playwright/test';
import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, assertNoJsError, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';

async function createRepo(page: Page) {
  const repoName = `e2e-shortcut-${randomString(8)}`;
  await apiCreateRepo(page.request, {name: repoName});
  await apiCreateFile(page.request, env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, repoName, 'other.txt', 'other file');
  return `/${env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER}/${repoName}`;
}

// presses a shortcut that leaves the page, and waits until the next page can take one
async function goWith(page: Page, keys: string, url: RegExp) {
  for (const key of keys.split(' ')) await page.keyboard.press(key);
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(url);
  await page.waitForLoadState();
}

test('s and t focus their boxes, and Escape clears them', async ({page}) => {
  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  const search = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]');
  const searchHint = page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd');
  const goToFile = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container input');
  const goToFileHint = page.locator('.repo-file-search-container kbd');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 't'); // the Vue box has mounted and registered
  await expect(searchHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');
  await expect(goToFileHint).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Repository');

  await page.keyboard.press('s');
  await expect(search).toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeHidden();
  await page.keyboard.type('st');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('st');
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(search).toHaveValue('');
  await expect(search).not.toBeFocused();
  await expect(searchHint).toBeVisible();

  await page.keyboard.press('t');
  await expect(goToFile).toBeFocused();
  await expect(goToFileHint).toBeHidden();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

  await page.goto(await createRepo(page));
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top kbd')).toHaveAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', 's'); // s is a live shortcut here
  await page.locator('aria-menu:has(.language-menu) > button').focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');

  await expect(page.locator('.language-menu .item:focus')).toHaveText(/^s/i);
  await expect(page.locator('.repo-home-sidebar-top input[name="q"]')).not.toBeFocused();
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

export function selectedCommentMarkup(selection: Selection | null): HTMLElement | null {
  if (!selection?.rangeCount || selection.isCollapsed) return null;
  const ancestor = selection.getRangeAt(0).commonAncestorContainer;
  const markup = (ancestor instanceof Element ? ancestor : ancestor.parentElement)?.closest<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup');
  // only a comment with raw content can be quoted, which leaves out the reply box's own preview
  if (!markup?.parentElement!.querySelector(':scope > .raw-content')) return null;
  return markup;
}

function focusReplyEditor(editor: ComboMarkdownEditor) {
  if (editor.tabEditor && !editor.tabEditor.classList.contains('active')) editor.switchTabToEditor(); // the Preview tab hides the cursor and any quote
  editor.focus();
  editor.moveCursorToEnd();
}

// shared by the "Quote reply" menu item and the "r" shortcut
function appendQuoteReply(editor: ComboMarkdownEditor, contentToQuote: string) {
  const quotedContent = `${contentToQuote.replace(/^/mg, '> ')}\\n\\n`;
  if (editor.value()) {
    editor.value(`${editor.value()}\\n\\n${quotedContent}`);
  } else {
    editor.value(quotedContent);
  }
  focusReplyEditor(editor);
}

async function tryOnQuoteReply(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.quote-reply');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const contentToQuoteId = clickTarget.getAttribute('data-target');
  const targetRawToQuote = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${contentToQuoteId}.raw-content`)!;
  const targetMarkupToQuote = targetRawToQuote.parentElement!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup')!;
  let contentToQuote = extractSelectedMarkdown(targetMarkupToQuote);
  if (!contentToQuote) contentToQuote = targetRawToQuote.textContent;

  let editor;
  if (clickTarget.classList.contains('quote-reply-diff')) {
    const replyBtn = clickTarget.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.comment-form-reply')!;
    editor = await handleReply(replyBtn);
  } else {
    // for normal issue/comment page
    editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  }
  appendQuoteReply(editor, contentToQuote);
}

// "r" exists only where the server rendered the reply form, so it needs no permission checks of its own
function initRepoIssueQuoteReplyShortcut(form: HTMLElement) {
  const editorContainer = form.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.combo-markdown-editor')!;
  registerShortcut({
    keys: form.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: form.getAttribute('data-shortcut-description')!,
    section: form.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section')!,
    element: editorContainer,
    action: () => {
      const editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(editorContainer);
      if (!editor) return; // still loading
      const markup = selectedCommentMarkup(window.getSelection());
      if (markup) {
        appendQuoteReply(editor, extractSelectedMarkdown(markup));
      } else {
        focusReplyEditor(editor);
      }
    },
  });
}

function select(start: Node, startOffset: number, end: Node, endOffset: number) {
  const range = document.createRange();
  range.setStart(start, startOffset);
  range.setEnd(end, endOffset);
  const selection = window.getSelection()!;
  selection.removeAllRanges();
  selection.addRange(range);
  return selection;
}

function text(root: HTMLElement, selector: string) {
  return root.querySelector(selector)!.firstChild!;
}

test('selectedCommentMarkup', () => {
  const root = createElementFromHTML(timeline);
  document.body.append(root);
  const first = root.querySelector('#first .markup');

  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#first p'), 5))).toBe(first);
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#first p:last-child'), 6))).toBe(first); // across paragraphs
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 2, text(root, '#first p'), 2))).toBeNull(); // collapsed
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#second p'), 5))).toBeNull(); // two comments
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#outside'), 0, text(root, '#outside'), 7))).toBeNull();
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(select(text(root, '#dismissed p'), 0, text(root, '#dismissed p'), 9))).toBeNull(); // no raw content to quote
  window.getSelection()!.removeAllRanges();
  expect(selectedCommentMarkup(window.getSelection())).toBeNull();
  root.remove();
});

test('r quotes the selection after the existing text, or only moves to the reply box', () => {
  const root = createElementFromHTML(timeline);
  const form = createElementFromHTML(`<form id="comment-form" data-shortcut-keys="r" data-shortcut-description="Quote Reply" data-shortcut-section="Conversation">
    <div class="combo-markdown-editor"></div>
  </form>`);
  document.body.append(root, form);
  let value = 'earlier text';
  const editor = {
    tabEditor: createElementFromHTML('<a class="item"></a>'), // the Preview tab is active
    value: (v?: string) => v === undefined ? value : (value = v),
    switchTabToEditor: vi.fn(() => editor.tabEditor.classList.add('active')),
    focus: vi.fn(),
    moveCursorToEnd: vi.fn(),
  };
  (form.querySelector('.combo-markdown-editor') as any)._giteaComboMarkdownEditor = editor;

  expect(getShortcuts()).toContainEqual({keys: 'r', description: 'Quote Reply', section: 'Conversation'});

  select(text(root, '#first p'), 0, text(root, '#first p:last-child'), 6);
  document.body.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key: 'r', bubbles: true}));
  expect(value).toBe('earlier text\n\n> first line\n> \n> second\n\n');
  expect(editor.switchTabToEditor).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  expect(editor.moveCursorToEnd).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

  window.getSelection()!.removeAllRanges();
  document.body.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key: 'r', bubbles: true}));
  expect(value).toBe('earlier text\n\n> first line\n> \n> second\n\n'); // unchanged
  expect(editor.switchTabToEditor).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); // already on the Write tab
  expect(editor.moveCursorToEnd).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);

  root.remove();
  form.remove();
  expect(getShortcuts()).not.toContainEqual(expect.objectContaining({keys: 'r'}));
});

export async function apiCreateIssue(
  requestContext: APIRequestContext,
  {owner, repo, title, body, projects, milestone, headers}: {
    owner: string;
    repo: string;
    title: string;
    body?: string;
    projects?: number[];
    milestone?: number;
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
  },
): Promise<{index: number}> {
  let result: {index: number} = {index: 0};
  await apiRetry(async () => {
    const response = await requestContext.post(`${baseUrl()}/api/v1/repos/${owner}/${repo}/issues`, {
      headers: headers || apiHeaders(),
      data: {title, body: body || '', projects: projects || [], ...(milestone && {milestone})},
    });
    if (response.ok()) {
      const json = await response.json();
      // API returns "number" field for the issue index
      result = {index: json.number};
    }
    return response;
  }, 'apiCreateIssue');
  return result;
}

export async function login(page: Page, username = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_USER, password = env.GITEA_TEST_E2E_PASSWORD) {
  const response = await page.request.post('/user/login', {
    form: {user_name: username, password},
    maxRedirects: 0,
  });
  const status = response.status();
  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
}

s=s.replace("import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateFile, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, assertNoJsError, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';",
"import {apiCreateBranch, apiCreateFile, apiCreateIssue, apiCreateRepo, apiEditRepo, assertNoJsError, login, randomString} from './utils.ts';")
s+='''
// an issue whose description is taller than the window, so the reply box starts out of view
async function createIssue(page: Page) {
  const repoLink = await createRepo(page);
  const [, owner, repoName] = repoLink.split('/');
  const filler = Array.from({length: 30}, (_, i) => `filler paragraph ${i}`).join('\\n\\n');
  await apiCreateIssue(page.request, {owner, repo: repoName, title: 'Quote test', body: `first line\\n\\nsecond line\\n\\n${filler}`});
  return {issueLink: `${repoLink}/issues/1`, owner, repoName};
}

test('r quotes the selected text into the reply box, or moves to it', async ({page}) => {
  await page.setViewportSize({width: 1280, height: 600});
  const [{issueLink}] = await Promise.all([createIssue(page), login(page)]);
  await page.goto(issueLink);
  const replyBox = page.getByPlaceholder('Leave a comment');
  await expect(page.locator('#comment-form')).toHaveAttribute('data-shortcut-section', 'Conversation');
  await expect(replyBox).not.toBeInViewport();

  await page.locator('.issue-content-left .render-content.markup').first().evaluate((markup) => {
    const range = document.createRange();
    range.setStart(markup.querySelector('p')!.firstChild!, 0);
    range.setEnd(markup.querySelectorAll('p')[1].firstChild!, 6);
    window.getSelection()!.addRange(range);
  });
  await page.keyboard.press('r');
  await expect(replyBox).toBeFocused();
  await expect(replyBox).toBeInViewport();
  await expect(replyBox).toHaveValue(/^> first line\\n> second\\n/);
  await page.keyboard.type('reply');
  await expect(replyBox).toHaveValue(/\\n\\nreply$/); // the cursor was after the quote, and r typed in the box is a letter
  const typed = await replyBox.inputValue();

  await replyBox.blur();
  await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
  await expect(replyBox).not.toBeInViewport();
  await page.keyboard.press('r'); // nothing selected
  await expect(replyBox).toBeFocused();
  await expect(replyBox).toBeInViewport();
  await expect(replyBox).toHaveValue(typed);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});

test('r does nothing without a reply box', async ({page}) => {
  const {issueLink, owner, repoName} = await createIssue(page);
  await page.goto(issueLink); // signed out
  await expect(page.locator('#comment-form')).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.keyboard.press('r');
  await assertNoJsError(page);

  await apiEditRepo(page.request, owner, repoName, {archived: true});
  await login(page);
  await page.goto(issueLink);
  await expect(page.locator('#comment-form')).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.keyboard.press('r');
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

`.claude/skills/verify/` was generated on 2026-10-06. It's local-only, because `.claude/` is gitignored.

- `bin/gitea-verify up|doctor|down|list` starts a dev-mode Gitea on a free port, with its own sqlite DB and a throwaway `verify-admin`.
- `doctor` warns when `./gitea` or `public/assets` is older than the source.
- `bin/drive.mjs` gives a signed-in Playwright session.
- Artifacts persist under `.claude/verify-runs/<id>/artifacts/`.
- The feature map has 10 features: the original seven plus notifications (#50/#51) and multi-select ARIA (#63), with shortcuts updated for #58's g keys and, on 2026-10-24, #57's `?` help dialog (extended in place, not a new feature). All were driven live on 2026-10-24 by pstack's `/maintain-verification-skill`, which the user has since uninstalled. Map upkeep now belongs to the local `verify-map` skill (`.claude/skills/verify-map/`). Its `add` mode maps a new feature (file, recipe, README line and mise task) and its `audit` mode checks source and drives everything live. `scripts/check-map.sh` checks that the four views agree.
- Since 2026-10-24 each feature has a saved, asserting recipe in `recipes/<feature>.mjs`, and `bin/verify-run` runs them. The user asked for a gitignored root `mise.toml` with `verify:*` tasks (trusted): `mise run verify:all` (~50 s serial since the 2026-10-24 audit added the missing entry points to six recipes) or `'verify:feature:*'` (~20 s parallel, one instance each). It has no `[tools]`, since the flake owns tools. mise's `sources`/`outputs` never skipped the builds (the outputs are gitignored), so make decides freshness. The user chose on 2026-10-24 to skip the mise MCP server. `mise run` through Bash streams output and picks up task edits; MCP only returns output when a task finishes, keeps a stale task list until restarted, and auto-accepts confirm prompts.
- On 2026-10-24 `gitea-verify up --owner <pid>` gained a watchdog (verify-run passes its own PID; teardown now survives SIGKILL), and `prune` (run by `up` first) cleans dead runs. A nushell port matched it but needs nushell in the flake; the user chose to keep bash. gitea-verify only kills a PID whose command line has this run's `web --config <run>/work/custom/conf/app.ini` (`ours()`); in the 2026-10-24 comparison it was the only version, against nushell and a Python + psutil port, that spared a reused PID in every case.
- `session({name, user, password})` signs the browser in as a second account; `api()` stays admin, so use `?sudo=<user>` for that user's API view.
- The SKILL.md already covers dev mode, `/devtest`, the Firefox hang, WebKit Tab skipping and the `networkidle` trap.

Traps it doesn't cover:
- **Firefox is CI-only.** Firefox 1532 hangs at launch on this Mac (macOS 27.0.1 `sandbox_extension_issue_file_to_process`), even outside Claude's sandbox, and there's no docker/podman for `PLAYWRIGHT_MODE=container`. Run e2e locally with `--project=chromium --project=webkit`, with the Claude sandbox disabled.
- **Two dropdowns on the appearance page.** `/user/settings/appearance` has two `.ui.selection.dropdown` elements, for theme and language. Scope to `form[action$="/theme"]`.
- **A modal `<dialog>` hides a missing key guard.** `showModal()` makes the page inert, so a focus shortcut like `s` can't fire behind it even with no guard. Prove a "no shortcuts while open" rule with a navigation key (`g i`) and a check that fails if the page navigates. Found on #57, where both the recipe and the e2e test first passed with the guard removed.
- **`make frontend` decides freshness, not doctor.** Doctor's stale-bundle WARN can persist after a rebuild when a source file is rewritten with identical content; check that `public/assets/.vite/manifest.json` is newer than the source.
- **Injecting markup.** `page.evaluate` can inject markup into any Gitea page and render it with real component CSS, which is useful without a populated repo.

**Why:** The user's own :3000 instance (`custom/conf/app.ini`, `data/`) and its accounts must not be disturbed. Driving a separate disposable instance avoids that.

Issue #95 is implemented in the working copy on top of fresh `main`, independent of #57. Nothing is committed yet, because the repo rules need your approval for each commit.

**What changed**
- **Shared quote helper** (`web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`): the quoting code from `tryOnQuoteReply` moved into `appendQuoteReply`, and `focusReplyEditor` handles focusing. Both the "Quote Reply" menu item and `r` use them. The helper switches the box back from Preview to Write (AC4), so the menu item gets that fix too, as the spec said it would.
- **When a selection counts:** `selectedCommentMarkup` accepts a selection only if it sits inside a single comment's rendered text and that comment has raw content to quote. Otherwise `r` just moves to the reply box with the text unchanged (AC3).
- **Registration** (Decision 2): `#comment-form` in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl` now carries `data-global-init` plus the shortcut's key, description and section. So `r` only exists where the server drew a reply form (AC5), and it goes away with the form.
  - The description reuses `repo.issues.context.quote_reply` ("Quote Reply").
  - For the section I reused `repo.pulls.tab_conversation` ("Conversation"), so no new locale key was needed. Say if you'd rather have a dedicated key.

**Tests**
- **Unit tests** (new `repo-issue-edit.test.ts`): the selection check for AC1 and AC3, plus the `r` action. That covers appending after existing text (AC2), the Preview-tab switch (AC4), the `getShortcuts()` entry (AC7) and the shortcut disappearing when the form leaves the page.
- **Playwright** (`tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts`): three new tests.

  - No reply box, for a signed-out visitor and for an archived repo (AC5).
  - A regression check that the menu item still quotes the whole comment and leaves the Preview tab.
